rules.rule_name: Medication Outside Validated Clinical Knowledge Base
rules.description: Prescribed medication is not present in the validated antimicrobial knowledge base; comprehensive safety checks (allergies, renal/hepatic adjustments, teratogenicity, interactions) cannot be evaluated.
rules.input_conditions: knowledge_base.get_drug_info(prescribed_drug) is None
rules.output_concern: Prescription safety evaluation unavailable — medication is outside the validated clinical knowledge base.
rules.recommendation: Perform manual clinical pharmacotherapy review before prescribing. Do not assume absence of contraindications or interactions.
rules.evidence_source: Clinical Decision Support Safety Architecture (Coverage Fail-Safe)
rules.guideline_version: System safeguard - not derived from a clinical guideline
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescribed antimicrobial is explicitly listed in ICMR guidelines as discouraged or avoided for empirical treatment of the diagnosed syndrome.
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed drug is in syndrome avoid_empirical list (e.g. Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin for uncomplicated cystitis).
rules.output_concern: Potential empirical guideline discordance identified. Agent is not recommended as first-line empirical therapy for this indication.
rules.recommendation: Review ICMR syndrome guideline. Consider first-line preferred agent (e.g. Nitrofurantoin or Fosfomycin for cystitis) or obtain culture/susceptibility results.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescribed medication matches an exact documented drug allergy in the patient's medical record.
rules.input_conditions: Patient has documented allergy matching the prescribed drug generic or brand name.
rules.output_concern: Potential direct medication allergy concern identified. Patient has documented allergy to this specific agent.
rules.recommendation: Review allergy history immediately. Prescribing this agent is contraindicated unless desensitization protocol or verified allergy delabeling is documented.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: AAAAI Drug Allergy Practice Parameter)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescribed medication belongs to the same structural class (e.g. Aminopenicillin) as documented allergy.
rules.input_conditions: Patient has penicillin class allergy and is prescribed a penicillin-class derivative (e.g. Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, Piperacillin).
rules.output_concern: Potential class-level beta-lactam allergy concern identified. Prescribed drug shares core beta-lactam ring / side-chain determinants.
rules.recommendation: Review allergy reaction severity (anaphylaxis/angioedema vs mild rash) and select non-beta-lactam alternative or consult allergy specialist.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters (JTFPP))
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED
unverified_sources: Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters (JTFPP)

rules.description: Patient has documented Penicillin allergy and is prescribed a Cephalosporin.
rules.input_conditions: Penicillin allergy present, prescribed Cephalosporin (1st/2nd gen ~5-10% cross-reactivity, 3rd/4th gen <1-2% cross-reactivity).
rules.output_concern: Potential cross-reactivity consideration identified between Penicillin allergy and prescribed Cephalosporin.
rules.recommendation: Review nature of prior penicillin reaction. 3rd-generation cephalosporins (e.g. Ceftriaxone) have low cross-reactivity (<1%) but require clinical vigilance if prior reaction was severe IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: AAAAI Drug Allergy Practice Parameter)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Patient allergy status is documented as unknown or unelicited.
rules.input_conditions: allergy_status_known == False or allergies is None/unrecorded.
rules.output_concern: Allergy assessment unavailable — patient allergy history has not been elicited.
rules.recommendation: Confirm allergy history with patient or family before administration. Do not assume absence of allergies.
rules.evidence_source: FDA Structured Product Label - amoxicillin (via NLM DailyMed). Re-cited from ICMR: no retrievable guideline passage on eliciting allergy history; stated verbatim in the amoxicillin label.
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED
rules.recited_note: no retrievable guideline passage on eliciting allergy history; stated verbatim in the amoxicillin label

rules.description: Patient's eGFR is below the threshold requiring dose reduction or interval extension for renally eliminated antimicrobials.
rules.input_conditions: Patient eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021 non-race) is below drug-specific clearance threshold (e.g., eGFR < 50 for Ciprofloxacin, < 30 for Amoxicillin).
rules.output_concern: Potential renal dosing consideration identified. Patient's renal filtration is reduced, risking drug accumulation and toxicity.
rules.recommendation: Review recommended renal dosage adjustment or extended dosing interval per clinical guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: Renal Drug Handbook)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Nitrofurantoin prescribed in patient with eGFR < 30 mL/min.
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed Nitrofurantoin AND eGFR < 30 mL/min.
rules.output_concern: Potential severe renal safety concern identified. Nitrofurantoin is ineffective for UTI and increases peripheral neuropathy risk when eGFR < 30 mL/min.
rules.recommendation: Review alternative urinary antimicrobial (e.g., Fosfomycin, Cefixime, or targeted agent based on culture) per ICMR UTI guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: AGS Beers Criteria)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Renally cleared antimicrobial prescribed when patient renal function (eGFR/creatinine) is unknown.
rules.input_conditions: renal_status_known == False or egfr_ml_min is None.
rules.output_concern: Renal dosing assessment unavailable — renal function information required for this renally cleared antimicrobial.
rules.recommendation: Obtain baseline serum creatinine / eGFR before starting or adjusting prolonged therapy. Do not assume normal renal function.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: KDIGO Guidelines)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.rule_name: Nitrofurantoin in Moderate Renal Impairment (Source Threshold Divergence)
rules.description: Nitrofurantoin prescribed when eGFR is between 30 and 59 mL/min. This band exists because the authoritative sources disagree: the FDA product label lists creatinine clearance under 60 mL/min as an absolute contraindication, while contemporary practice and the project's ICMR-derived threshold permit use down to 30 mL/min. The system surfaces the divergence at MODERATE severity rather than silently adopting either threshold.
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed Nitrofurantoin AND eGFR >= 30 AND eGFR < 60 mL/min.
rules.output_concern: Potential renal dosing consideration. Source thresholds diverge for this eGFR range: FDA product labelling treats CrCl < 60 mL/min as a contraindication, whereas the ICMR-derived threshold used by this system flags only below 30 mL/min. Both positions are surfaced for clinician judgement.
rules.recommendation: Review the divergence in the evidence panel. Consider an alternative urinary antimicrobial if the patient is close to the lower bound, has declining function, or has risk factors for peripheral neuropathy or pulmonary toxicity. Clinician judgement governs which threshold applies.
rules.evidence_source: FDA Structured Product Label (nitrofurantoin) vs ICMR-derived system threshold
rules.guideline_version: FDA SPL version per attached label; ICMR Treatment Guidelines 2nd edition (2019)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Patient with moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C) prescribed heavily hepatically metabolized antimicrobial.
rules.input_conditions: Child-Pugh Class B or C AND prescribed drug is Metronidazole, Voriconazole, or Rifampin.
rules.output_concern: Potential hepatic dosing consideration identified. Impaired hepatic clearance may cause toxic drug accumulation.
rules.recommendation: Review dose adjustment (e.g. 50% dose reduction for Metronidazole in Child-Pugh C) and monitor clinical signs of drug toxicity.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: British National Formulary)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Patient hepatic status is unknown when prescribed agent requiring hepatic clearance monitoring.
rules.input_conditions: hepatic_status_known == False AND drug has hepatic warnings.
rules.output_concern: Hepatic dosing assessment unavailable — hepatic function information required.
rules.recommendation: Review clinical history for liver disease or obtain baseline LFTs if patient has risk factors for hepatic impairment.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Simultaneous prescription of multiple agents providing overlapping anaerobic spectrum (e.g. Metronidazole + Piperacillin-Tazobactam).
rules.input_conditions: Prescription includes Metronidazole AND (Piperacillin-Tazobactam OR Meropenem OR Clindamycin OR Amoxicillin-Clavulanate).
rules.output_concern: Potential antimicrobial duplication identified. Dual redundant anaerobic coverage detected without documented clinical synergy.
rules.recommendation: Review regimen. Piperacillin-Tazobactam already provides potent anaerobic activity against Bacteroides spp.; Metronidazole is usually redundant unless central nervous system penetration is specifically required.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: IDSA Guidelines)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Simultaneous prescription of two antimicrobials from the same chemical super-class (e.g. two fluoroquinolones or two beta-lactams).
rules.input_conditions: Multiple drugs sharing identical super_class (e.g. Ciprofloxacin + Levofloxacin, or Amoxicillin + Ceftriaxone in non-synergistic indications).
rules.output_concern: Potential same-class antimicrobial duplication identified. Regimen contains multiple agents of the same pharmacological class.
rules.recommendation: Review indication and streamline regimen to a single appropriate antimicrobial agent.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes / The WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic book
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescription of Ciprofloxacin, Levofloxacin, Metronidazole, or Clarithromycin in a patient receiving Warfarin therapy.
rules.input_conditions: Patient active medication includes Warfarin AND prescribed antimicrobial is Ciprofloxacin, Metronidazole, Levofloxacin, or Clarithromycin.
rules.output_concern: Potential drug-drug interaction identified. Antimicrobial inhibits Warfarin metabolism / alters gut flora, significantly elevating INR and major bleeding risk.
rules.recommendation: Clinician review recommended. Obtain baseline INR, monitor INR at 48-72 hours, or consider alternative antimicrobial with lower interaction profile (e.g. Ceftriaxone/Amoxicillin).
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: CHEST Antithrombotic Guidelines)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescription of a QT-prolonging antimicrobial (Fluoroquinolones, Macrolides) in a patient taking concurrent QT-prolonging medication (Ondansetron, Amiodarone, Haloperidol).
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed drug is (Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, Ciprofloxacin, Levofloxacin) AND concurrent medication includes (Ondansetron, Amiodarone, Haloperidol, Methadone, Sotalol).
rules.output_concern: Potential cardiac drug-drug interaction identified. Concurrent use carries additive QT-interval prolongation risk with potential for Torsades de Pointes.
rules.recommendation: Review cardiac history, assess baseline QTc, correct hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, or substitute with non-QT prolonging agent (e.g. Beta-lactam / non-QT antiemetic).
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: AHA Scientific Statement, CredibleMeds QT Drugs Database)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Prescription of Linezolid in a patient taking SSRIs, SNRIs, or other serotonergic medications.
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed Linezolid AND concurrent medication includes (Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Escitalopram, Citalopram, Paroxetine, Venlafaxine, Duloxetine).
rules.output_concern: Potential critical drug-drug interaction identified. Linezolid is an MAOI; co-administration with serotonergic agents causes life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome.
rules.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. If Linezolid is strictly required for MDR Gram-positive infection, hold SSRI/SNRI and monitor for clonus, hyperthermia, and agitation per ICMR guidance.
rules.evidence_source: FDA Structured Product Label - linezolid (via NLM DailyMed). Re-cited from ICMR: serotonergic interaction is absent from the guideline corpus (0 occurrences of 'serotonin'); stated in the linezolid label.
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED
rules.recited_note: serotonergic interaction is absent from the guideline corpus (0 occurrences of 'serotonin'); stated in the linezolid label

rules.description: Prescription of Clarithromycin or high-dose Azithromycin in a patient receiving Atorvastatin or Simvastatin.
rules.input_conditions: Prescribed Clarithromycin/Azithromycin AND concurrent medication includes Atorvastatin/Simvastatin.
rules.output_concern: Potential drug interaction identified. Macrolides inhibit CYP3A4-mediated statin clearance, increasing risk of statin-induced myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
rules.recommendation: Temporarily hold statin during short antimicrobial course or select an alternative antibiotic (e.g. Amoxicillin/Doxycycline).
rules.evidence_source: FDA Structured Product Label - clarithromycin (via NLM DailyMed). Re-cited from ICMR: statin interaction is absent from the guideline corpus (0 occurrences of 'rhabdomyolysis'); stated in the clarithromycin label.
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED
rules.recited_note: statin interaction is absent from the guideline corpus (0 occurrences of 'rhabdomyolysis'); stated in the clarithromycin label

rules.rule_name: Fluoroquinolone Teratogenicity & Cartilage Risk in Pregnancy
rules.description: Prescription of Ciprofloxacin or Levofloxacin in a pregnant or lactating patient.
rules.input_conditions: pregnancy_status in ['PREGNANT_TRIMESTER_1', 'PREGNANT_TRIMESTER_2', 'PREGNANT_TRIMESTER_3'] AND prescribed drug is Fluoroquinolone.
rules.output_concern: Potential pregnancy safety concern identified. Fluoroquinolones carry risk of fetal cartilage toxicity and arthropathy.
rules.recommendation: Review safer alternative therapies in pregnancy (e.g. Beta-lactams, Cephalosporins) per ICMR Obstetric Antimicrobial Guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: ACOG Practice Bulletin)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.rule_name: Tetracycline Fetal Bone / Dental Staining Risk in Pregnancy
rules.description: Prescription of Doxycycline in a pregnant patient (2nd/3rd trimester).
rules.input_conditions: pregnancy_status in ['PREGNANT_TRIMESTER_2', 'PREGNANT_TRIMESTER_3'] AND prescribed drug is Doxycycline/Tetracycline.
rules.output_concern: Potential severe pregnancy teratogenicity concern identified. Tetracyclines cross placenta, causing permanent fetal dental discoloration, enamel dysplasia, and bone growth retardation.
rules.recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Review alternative pregnancy-safe antimicrobial per ICMR guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes / FDA Structured Product Label (via NLM DailyMed)
rules.guideline_version: 2nd edition (2019); per-drug SPL version, recorded on each attached label
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Antimicrobial prescribed for a pediatric patient without weight-based dosing verification.
rules.input_conditions: age_category == 'PEDIATRIC' OR age < 18.
rules.output_concern: Pediatric dosing review required. Pediatric antimicrobial dosing must be strictly calculated per kg body weight (mg/kg/day).
rules.recommendation: Verify patient weight in kg and ensure prescribed dose matches recommended mg/kg/day schedule per Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) / ICMR guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: IAP Drug Formulary)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.description: Female patient of childbearing age with unknown pregnancy status prescribed an agent with fetal toxicity risks.
rules.input_conditions: pregnancy_status == 'UNKNOWN' AND sex == 'FEMALE' AND age >= 12 AND age <= 50 AND prescribed drug has pregnancy warnings.
rules.output_concern: Pregnancy status unconfirmed for female patient of childbearing potential receiving antimicrobial with potential teratogenic considerations.
rules.recommendation: Confirm pregnancy/lactation status before dispensing. Do not assume non-pregnant state.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (additional authorities cited without a document in this repository: ACOG Practice Bulletin)
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.rule_name: WHO Reserve Group Antimicrobial Stewardship Alert
rules.description: Prescription of a WHO Reserve group antimicrobial (e.g. Linezolid, Colistin) requiring infectious disease pre-authorization.
rules.input_conditions: prescribed drug is classified as WHO RESERVE.
rules.output_concern: Antimicrobial stewardship alert: Prescribed agent is in the WHO 'RESERVE' category (last-resort antibiotic).
rules.recommendation: Review microbiology culture and sensitivity data. Reserve antibiotics should be protected and restricted to confirmed MDR pathogens per ICMR / WHO stewardship protocols.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes / The WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic book
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

rules.rule_name: Empirical Broad-Spectrum Watch Group Escalation Alert
rules.description: Use of WHO Watch group broad-spectrum agent (e.g. Meropenem, Ceftriaxone, Levofloxacin) for mild outpatient infections.
rules.input_conditions: Diagnosis is mild outpatient condition (e.g. Acute Bronchitis, Uncomplicated Cystitis) AND prescribed drug is WHO WATCH or RESERVE.
rules.output_concern: Antimicrobial stewardship consideration: Broad-spectrum Watch agent prescribed for mild/moderate indication where Access agents are first-line.
rules.recommendation: Review whether first-line Access antimicrobial (e.g. Amoxicillin, Nitrofurantoin, Doxycycline) is clinically appropriate per ICMR empirical guidelines.
rules.evidence_source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes / The WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic book
rules.author: SYSTEM_GENERATED

version_reconciliation_note: Rule citations reconciled against documents actually held in this repository. The ICMR source INGESTED and hash-verified here is the 2nd edition (2019); rule-level evidence therefore cites 2019 and must not be presented as any later edition. UPDATE 2026-08-23: seven chapters of the ICMR 2022-23 edition (intra-abdominal, skin and soft tissue, bone and joint, CNS, urinary tract, hospital acquired, immunocompromised host) are now held as operator-attested TRANSCRIPTIONS and indexed in icmr_stg_2022_23_syndromes.json. They are not the official PDF, carry no verifiable page numbers, and cover only part of the guideline, so the earlier statement that the 2022-23 edition 'is not present' is superseded but the rule catalog still cites 2019 for evidence. Authorities listed in unverified_sources are named in clinical rationale but have no ingested document and must not be presented to a clinician as retrievable evidence.
